clue.text: Clothing hotel could supply in southwest city not right for Robert?

parts.note: Bath is a city in southwest England

indicators.note: not means the letters for right are left out of the name Robert

parts.note: taken as the name written out in full

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about whether a Bath hotel would hand Robert something to wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a spa city in southwest England, so a bathrobe there fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathrobe is a towelling gown that many hotels leave in the room for guests to wear.

clue.text: Content to leave Eton, learner first to join up

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside letters, and they leave, so only the two ends of Eton remain

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation
1ST is the short form of first, with the figure 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: An Eton pupil quits the school, an L-plate learner being the first to sign up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'content' of Eton is its middle, TO; the figure 1 in 1ST is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign on for military service, the same as joining up.

clue.text: Embassy official's qualification document ahead of time

indicators.note: ahead of puts the document in front of the letter for time

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate awarded for a qualification

explanation.surface: An embassy official shows off a certificate before the deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is a state's representative abroad, typically working out of an embassy.

clue.text: Brought up beer: a mistake

indicators.note: in a down answer, brought up means the word for the beer is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: pils is short for pilsner, a pale lager beer

explanation.surface: Someone sicked up their beer, which was a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought up' looks like vomiting; in a down clue it means writing PILS bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small error or blunder, as in a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Small part of Society? Of course

parts.note: natch is informal slang for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: Someone asks if something is just a small part of Society, and the answer is: naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' looks like it gives S, but it belongs with 'part' as the definition; Society provides the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a brief fragment, as in a snatch of song or conversation.

clue.text: Extremely fickle sailors in plant

indicators.note: extremely points to the extreme letters, the first and last, of fickle

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy, i.e. sailors

explanation.surface: Changeable sailors aboard a plant, or caught up in one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a flowerless green plant with feathery fronds that spreads by spores.

clue.text: Rule, new, for grassy area

parts.note: a rule is a law

explanation.surface: A newly made rule about the grassy area, perhaps keep off the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawn is a stretch of mown turf in a garden or park.

clue.text: Manxman, eg, I defame in speech?

parts.note: slander is defamation that is spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A Manxman confesses to badmouthing someone out loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' tempts you to look for a soundalike, but it narrows 'defame' to its spoken form. A Manxman comes from the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman lives on the Isle of Man, so he is an example of an island dweller.

clue.text: Sound of birds warbling outside hotel that's exciting

definitions.note: a phrase standing for a noun: a thing that's exciting

indicators.note: outside means the birds' sound wraps around the letter for hotel

parts.note: a trill is the quavering sound birds make when warbling
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Birdsong heard outside a hotel is a thrilling experience.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrill is a sudden rush of excitement, or something that gives one.

clue.text: Tolerating delay saying goodbye to island, that's clear

indicators.note: saying goodbye to the island means its letter departs from the word

parts.note: someone tolerating delay is patient

explanation.surface: Someone putting up with a hold-up bids farewell to an island, and that's obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent as an adjective means obvious or plainly evident, as in a patent lie.

clue.text: Many old assault threats initially — prevented by this?

definitions.text: Many old assault threats initially — prevented by this?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each of the four words before it

explanation.surface: Many attacks in the past were kept out by a defensive ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters spell the answer, and the whole clue describes what it did: a water-filled trench that held off attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat is a water-filled ditch round a castle, built to stop besiegers reaching the walls.

clue.text: Hell! Limo hit pile of earth

indicators.note: the limo is hit, knocked out of shape, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A curse as a limousine crashes into a heap of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A molehill is the small mound of soil a mole throws up while tunnelling.

clue.text: See with help of this US city politician linked with job?

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
MP is a Member of Parliament
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles politician is connected with a job, as if a scandal story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamppost holds a street light, which lets people see in the dark.

clue.text: What might be supplied by the 22 — exotic lagers, South European

definitions.text: What might be supplied by the 22

indicators.note: exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of lagers are rearranged

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: Someone generous hands out unusual lagers in southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The 22 is 22-across, GENEROUS: a generous person supplies largesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is liberal giving of money or gifts, exactly what a generous benefactor provides.

clue.text: Enthusiasm about Queen meeting cricketer? Exactly as stated

indicators.note: about means the word for enthusiasm goes around the other pieces

parts.note: vim is energy and enthusiasm

indicators.note: meeting puts the Queen directly alongside the cricketer

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: Royal enthusiasm about meeting a cricketer, reported word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbatim means in exactly the same words as were originally used.

clue.text: One producing beer outside of Renfrew in new way?

definitions.text: One producing beer outside of Renfrew in new way?

indicators.note: set out in a new way, so the letters of beer and the two outside letters are rearranged
the outside of a word is its first and last letters, here of Renfrew

explanation.surface: A beer maker from Scotland trying a new method beyond Renfrew.
explanation.walkthrough: BEER and RW, the outside of Renfrew, are mixed together; the whole clue describes the answer. Renfrew is a town near Glasgow.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer is a person or company that makes beer.

clue.text: Chloe rang regularly — a warning?

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the second

explanation.surface: Chloe phoned at regular intervals, perhaps as a caution.
explanation.definitionFit: A car horn is sounded to alert others to danger, so it serves as a warning.

clue.text: Announce woman's with a lord

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman is out with a nobleman, as society news might report.
explanation.definitionFit: To herald is to proclaim or signal that something is coming.

clue.text: Part of Attica then — some city!

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piece of ancient Attica, back then, was some city.
explanation.definitionFit: Athens is the Greek capital, the chief city of the region of Attica.

clue.text: Section of account we excise as over-sentimental

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An editor cuts part of a report for being too mawkish.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for quaint in a cloying, sickly sweet way.

clue.text: Small auction item in assigned position

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a lot is an item put up for sale at auction

explanation.surface: A little lot at auction sits in its allotted place in the catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: A slot is an allotted place in a schedule or sequence.

clue.text: Grain crop — pressure to replace British — confer

indicators.note: to replace says the letter for pressure takes the place of the letter for British

parts.note: barley is a cereal crop
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Farmers discuss grain prices with pressure to swap out British produce.
explanation.definitionFit: To parley is to hold talks, especially with an opponent, to settle terms.

clue.text: Doctor urges one to become willing to give

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A physician presses a patient to become a donor.
explanation.definitionFit: A generous person is open-handed and freely shares money or time.

clue.text: In the end, will you miss much person drinking a lot?

indicators.note: in the end points to the end letter of each of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether, ultimately, you will miss a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Lush is informal British for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is slang for a habitual drunkard, someone who drinks heavily.
